productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I needed a laptop that can handle my accessibility needs.  I use Magnifier and a screen reader, which can be rather taxing on a system.  When I was researching this product, one of the first YouTube reviews that came up was some guy bashing this product.  But I kept watching other reviews and reading.  I wound up by giving it a chance.  I'm glad I did. The first video review I saw where the guy was bashing it, was comparing it to something twice the price or more... which is not fair to do.This laptop is actually VERY nice.  It's sturdy, not flimsy, which was a big selling point for me, since my school-age daughter and I aren't the most graceful people on the planet.  It's got a 16 inch nice crispy display, with a full keyboard, including a numpad.  The key travel isn't quite that of an external keyboard, but MUCH better key travel than many other laptops.  I can actually type on this thing.  It's got plenty of USB ports, an HDMI out, combo headphone/mic 3.5mm port, etc., and even has an Ethernet port.If you're going to get this, I would suggest a couple things:Get an extra 8GB of RAM for it.As soon as Windows is done installing and setting up itself, remove the bloatware like McAfee and most of the ASUS services.  They're completely unnecessary, and only serve to take resources away from what you want to be doing instead.  You can always re-install the ASUS stuff later if you need to modify or diagnose stuff.Go to Windows Update and get the latest drivers for the chipsets.So far, I don't have any major complaints.  It runs everything I've thrown at it, including games like ESO and Star Wars: Outlaw.Is it a $3000 Alienware uber-spec'ed wet dream?  No.  It's a fully capable, well built gaming laptop.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: TLDR: ASUS laptops have been solid for me. Do your research though!
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: The ASUS computers have been solid computers for mid tier gaming and designs. We have got several over the past few years. When choosing which one Get the CPU/GPU, graft a card, and screen size you want. You can upgrade memory and SSD to fit your goals.Based on others reviews I had seen some of the models sold by 3rd parties can potentially have some defects. But those seem hit or miss as any mass production item can have some faulty hardware.My recommendation: I prefer the GPU over CPU with 5-7 cores. And a decent graphics card. I usually go NVIDA for the card. Unless you want to get the best get one that is a year or two older. They can still crank up graphics pretty well and save you some money. I can’t say for sure what the sweet spot is for model numbers as those change frequently.Windows 11 is the best long term choice even though I’d stay Windows 10 If that was feasible. But it’s not.I’d recommend getting at least 32Gb of Ram  for gaming. Whether you desire to spend more now or save now and upgrade later. The choice is yours. 16gb will let you play games but not have the beat graffiti settings.As for the SSD if your laptop doesn’t have an additional slot. You can clone your SSD and replace it. I just replaced my 500gb to go to 2tb. I’d say don’t go less than 500gb to start.  If you do like to download a lot of games and have videos or video editing the more space you have is always better.  SSD cards have a read write speed. The better that speed is the quicker apps and games load up and process.I hope this helps!

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Great GPU Upgrade for Some but Not All
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: So far, so good!TLDR; Affordable, well packaged, easy  install, solid upgrade for pre-built integrated graphics computers with smaller power supplies, and/or cases with size constraints, will help provide more available RAM for CPU/system tasks.Disclaimer: I am not a gamer, my main use case is 3D modeling/business/productivity, the computer that was upgraded is an HP ENVY TE-01 3254 with an Intel i7-127000 12th gen, 32 GB RAM, 1TB SSDThe HP ENVY has some real limitations in upgrading the GPU due to the small stock power supply (310W) and size constraints of the case. I considered upgrading the power supply and getting a higher powered GPU, but for my needs it wasn't absolutely necessary. So, I opted for the RTX 3050 6GB based on price, and ease of installation with no external power needed as it receives all power needed from the PCIe slot itself.The apps that I'm using most are Autodesk Revit and AutoCAD, sometimes Sketchup, and the Adobe Suite, mostly Acrobat Pro, Illustrator, InDesign, and Photoshop. In general these apps use a lot of system memory, but have also benefited from the updated GPU. I've used Revit with various computers over the years, and it performed decently with the built-in graphics card, but the RTX 3050 (or any dedicated GPU) is definitely snappier and everything looks more crisp. I'm not doing a lot of rendering, if you're using a dedicated rendering engine for Revit or Sketchup, the more VRAM you have, the better.One definite benefit after adding the RTX 3050 is the availability of system RAM. In Task Manager, I was always seeing 85% or more of Memory Usage with multiple apps open. With the RTX 3050 that has dropped down to around 50-60% which is great for the overall stability of the system while providing more available memory for the CPU. The GPU is operating around 35-40 degrees Celsius and I don't notice the fans unless I put my ear right by the CPU tower.I know the 3050 is a much maligned GPU by many in the gamer and tech community and there are generally much better options for that user base, but I'm extremely pleased with my purchase. A few tips for those with minimal experience in upgrading their computers: set a system restore point before the install, be sure to remove all of the peels from the GPU prior to install, it has a lot of them and was packaged exceptionally well; the computer should recognize the GPU after restart, sometimes you might need to unplug an plug the monitor cable into the new GPU,  it will usually disable onboard graphics if applicable; then you can install the NVIDIA app and GPU Tweak 3 to customize your settings.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Great Laptop. Things to note, especially for intel users.Great Laptop. Things to note, especially for intel users.
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: When I first opened the box, I found that the laptop had a relatively solid build quality. Even for plastic, the solid quality to it doesn't make it feel flimsy or loose to type into. Some minor flex is noticed, but doesn’t make it feel "hollow" or cheap either. Two days into continuous usage and some stress tests and I'm contented to how snappy it feels. The i7 model I went may be a little bit of an overkill, but it is more than enough for anything. (The i5 model runs out of stock pretty quick.) For someone who came from a Surface Pro 4 i5 and MBA, the build quality is rather impressive for the years I have owned aluminum-based devices. I have not really experienced any serious issues with gaming either. The Lenovo Vantage app is a great touch and I was able to optimize the usage I have for my computer. Speakers were decently capable, and I was able to tune it out using the Nahimic program. The 120hz display is silky smooth and clear with its anti-glare surface.Bottlenecks, Recommendations + NOTES:Upgrading the RAM helps...but is rather necessary. I experienced some lag in some areas when I had a lot of programs opened, including FPS drops when I played games requiring a lot of memory. Task Manager showed consistent 40% or more RAM being used. I strongly advise others to focus on upgrading the RAM to at least 16GB to prevent lagging and some potential crashes in other software. Keep in mind, the RAM it uses for intel (both i5 and i7) model laptops is DDR4, which isn't the best, but a great performer nonetheless..Just unusual that the Ryzen version has a MOBO that uses DDR5. I recommend getting 3200MHz to get most out of the performance you need for the RAM. The "16GB" limit stated from the manufacturer is uncertain, the possibility to use 32, or even 64GB of RAM should work.The storage is decent, however the 512GB may not be enough especially for gaming. So I recommend upgrading the memory. NOTE: It is necessary to use the smaller M.2 (2242) SSD (gen 4 capable) if you don't intend to replace the stock 512GB M.2, as it occupies 2280 M.2 already (for what I know about intel)The display of this laptop is good. It could definitely be better, but for everyday tasks and gaming it does more than enough for what I need. I don't highly recommend doing art/design related work on it, as the colors aren't going to be impressive for this laptop, they are okay at the best. I recommend getting a separate display for that. Some light bleed may be noticed on a very dark background as well.Battery life may also be lacking if the user uses extensive graphics in this computer. It is decent for the most part, and could possibly range from the least 2-7 depending on how it is being used and the specification it has. I'm yet to run out of battery since I have kept it charged in most cases. I don't travel that much either.Note: To mitigate with battery life, I recommend opening the Vantage app to switch the power mode to "Hybrid-Auto" mode, so it switches to the integrated graphics when unplugged for lower power usage. Unless you intend to game, you may put it back to Hybrid mode. I also recommend switching the thermal mode to "quiet" mode, so it reduces performance that may hinder battery life. The hotkey Fn-Q can switch power modes seamlessly. Which is indicated by the power button LED.I highly recommend updating all drivers as well.I bought this laptop in mind to use it long term and for moderate tasks and not solely for its gaming purposes. Overall, it is value for price, definitely needs upgrades though.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I'm rating this laptop based on it's specs, not compared to all available specs. With that said, I'll keep it simple. For what it is, it's great. I bought it for a family member that doesn't play the most up to date games so it'll definitely handle anything they need where the graphics card is concerned.There are two things however. The RAM is still low. 8gb just isn't that much. A lot of games suggest 16 but even outside of gaming, open enough Chrome, Firefox, etc tabs and you'll use up 8 pretty quick. The good news is another 8gb stick is about 20 bucks.Storage is also rather small by today's standards. 512gb. Half of that was used up within a couple hours between the operating system (windows 11) and the first couple games. This is where things get pricier. A half decent NVME SSD will average around 80-100 dollars per terabyte (1024gb). Faster ones may cost a little more depending on the brand.So long as you know what you're buying, it's good. I highly suggest adding RAM for $20. As for more SSD space, it's questionable. If you're patient, you could easily get a decent sized external drive to swap programs on for a lot less than another NVME but, don't expect it to be near as fast.This computer is fairly sleek. Boots fast. Runs kind of loud but not in a concerning way. The battery life is decent. For the price you'll have a hard time finding much better if you're looking at a laptop purely gaming related (that is, at this time given that prices drop fast).

productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewTitle: Excelente laptop para su rango de precio, entendiendo que tiene limitaciones
productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewDescription: Sacándola de la caja, esta laptop tiene dos puntos negativos que son obvios: la paupérrima, terrible y dolorosa cantidad de RAM (es prácticamente inutilizable) y la duración corta de su batería.Sin embargo, el primer punto negativo es algo que fácilmente se supera comprando un kit de memoria DDR4 para portátiles. Cabe señalar que se le pueden instalar hasta 64 GB de RAM en dos módulos de 32 GB. Y no, Lenovo no recomienda ni dice que la máxima cantidad de RAM es 16 GB. En la especificación detallada lo que dice es que 16 GB de RAM es la cantidad máxima con la que Lenovo vende una variante de esta laptop, nada más. Yo llevó un año usándola con 32 GB de RAM. Solamente la encendí una vez con sus tristísimos 8 GB de RAM de fábrica. Si no le van a poner más RAM, entonces busquen otra laptop.Por otro lado, un punto sumamente agradable es que el SSD que incluye está ocupando el slot pequeño, y no el más estándar de 80 mm (M.2 2280), así que es muy fácil que quede con dos SSDs y así no dejar de aprovechar el que ya incluye. El slot 2280 también es PCIe Gen 4 (por ahí andan datos falsos volando que dicen que es Gen 3), así que se va a calentar si le instalan uno rápido, y la laptop no trae un pad térmico extra para este slot, por lo que les recomiendo que compren un disipador de metal delgado para laptop (aquí en Amazon venden unos) o al menos un pad térmico ancho que alcance a hacer contacto con el metal de la tapa.En cuestión del display, pues cumple y ya; nada sobresaliente. El sonido es mediocre. La batería es mala (ya lo había mencionado). Y la laptop se siente decente al tacto; es lo suficientemente sólida. En estos aspectos, cumple con lo que se puede esperar de un modelo de su gama, excepto por, tal vez, su batería.En conclusión, esta laptop tiene una excelente relación calidad-precio, y para quienes saben qué esperar de ella, es una muy buena compra; pero no se la puedo recomendar a todos porque sus 8 GB de RAM iniciales la hacen inutilizable para quienes no están dispuestos a hacerle la mejora.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Acer Nitro 5 AN515-55-53E5 - Budget Gaming Excellence
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I've own three Acer Nitro 5 AN515-55-53E5 Gaming Laptops, and I can confidently say that this model represents the best gaming laptop you can get on a budget from Amazon. Here's why:Performance: The heart of this laptop is the Intel Core i5-10300H, a quad-core processor with a base clock speed of 2.5 GHz that can turbo boost up to 4.5 GHz. Paired with the NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3050 GPU, which features 2nd Gen Ray Tracing Cores and 3rd Gen Tensor Cores, this laptop offers robust performance for gaming at 1080p. The RTX 3050 supports DLSS (Deep Learning Super Sampling), which significantly boosts frame rates without sacrificing visual quality. My experience shows that it handles modern games like "Cyberpunk 2077" and "Assassin's Creed Valhalla" at medium to high settings with very playable frame rates, often exceeding 60 FPS for less demanding titles.Cooling: One of the standout features is the cooling system. Acer's CoolBoost technology enhances fan speed by 10% and increases CPU/GPU cooling by 9% compared to auto mode, leading to a 25% overall boost in thermal performance. This means even during extended gaming sessions, the laptop maintains stable performance without thermal throttling. The dual fans, combined with a thoughtful chassis design that allows for good airflow, keep the system cool under pressure.Design: The Nitro 5's design is both functional and appealing. The chassis is made of matte black plastic with red accents, offering a subtle yet recognizable gaming aesthetic. It's sturdy for its price range, with just a slight flex on the keyboard deck and lid. The laptop weighs about 5.07 lbs (2.29 kg), which is reasonable for a 15.6-inch machine with these specifications. The keyboard features a red backlit design with a comfortable key travel, ideal for long gaming sessions.Display and Audio: The 15.6-inch Full HD IPS display has a 144Hz refresh rate, providing smooth visuals, which is crucial for gaming, especially in fast-paced environments. While the color gamut isn't the widest, the contrast and brightness are adequate for gaming and general use. Audio from the built-in speakers is surprisingly decent for this price point, though, as with most laptops, headphones or external speakers will enhance the experience.Battery Life and Connectivity: Battery life isn't the laptop’s strong suit, typically lasting around 3-4 hours on light usage and significantly less under gaming load. However, the convenience of features like USB 3.2 Gen 2 Type-C, HDMI 2.0, and Wi-Fi 6 more than compensates for this. The inclusion of a Killer Ethernet E2600 for wired connections ensures low-latency gaming when possible.Personal Experience: Having three of these laptops, I've found them to be reliable workhorses for both gaming and productivity tasks. The upgradability, with easy access to RAM and storage, makes them future-proof to some extent. They've been flawless in operation, with no hardware issues to report, making them an excellent choice for gamers on a budget or anyone seeking a cost-effective, high-performance laptop.In summary, the Acer Nitro 5 AN515-55-53E5 stands out for its balance of performance, cooling efficiency, and design at a budget-friendly price, making it a top pick for anyone looking to dive into gaming without breaking the bank. Five stars for delivering beyond expectations.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Good sub-$1000 gaming laptops are hard to find, but The Nitro 5 gives great value without breaking the bank.  The 10th Gen Core i5 processor is 2 generations old at this point, but it has plenty of power to run pretty much all modern games at a decent setting.  The Nvidia RTX 3050 graphics processor is an entry level to the new Ray-Tracing sexiness that's the next big thing in graphics.  On newer games you probably won't be able to get past the 60fps barrier at 1080p with the settings cranked, but dialing the details down a bit will give you better rates. The display is rated for 1080p and 144hz, and while it's not the brightest or most vibrant screen out there, it's fine for this price point.  There is also a (full size) HDMI out, but I have not had occasion to connect this to an external monitor yet.  The cooling fans do a good job of keeping this machine within temp specs... but do note they can get pretty loud under load (honestly that's almost inevitable on a gaming laptop, it's hard to keep things cool in such a small box. Anyone who games on a laptop should invest in a good headset IMHO.)I have opened this computer up to install a few upgrades (more on that below) and I will say I'm pretty impressed with the build quality for a computer in this segment.  The components are reputable makes rather than mystery off-brands (WD for the SSD, looks like Micron on the single 8gb RAM stick.) All the panels fit together nice and go back together easily after disassembly, making upgrades something you don't have to dread.Speaking of those upgrades... for a computer at this price point you have to live with a few compromises and here is where they may be found.  The storage this model comes with is a paltry 256gb m.2 drive... If you do plan on gaming on the Nitro, either be ready to upgrade this quickly or learn to love delete-ing and re-installing games and apps constantly.  Fortunately, there is a second un-used m.2 PCIe slot on the motherboard to accommodate an upgrade (this processor and motherboard supports PCIe up to gen-3 speeds.) There is also an open 2.5 inch bay for an SSD. Memory-wise, this unit comes with a single 8gb DDR4 SODIMM RAM stick installed.  This should be fine for most gaming- if you don't run big apps in the background-  but since this has two slots total for an upgrade I removed it and installed 2 8gb sticks of Kingston FURY Impact DDR4 RAM,  just for a bit of extra headroom (the max speed the i5 10300H will operate memory at is 2933 Mhz, so it's not worth it to spend more on faster RAM.)All in all, this is a fine machine for someone who's interested in a good no-fuss entryway into PC gaming, or a seasoned gamer who wants an inexpensive but capable machine to go mobile with. Highly Recommended!

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Despite its quirks its a solid machine
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I've had this laptop now since Aug of 2022 and I have to say that overall, it's been worth the money. For an everyday machine with a bit of extra kick it can do a lot. For a mid-level gamer or someone who does some lighter end video/photo editing it will get the job done.Since I purchased it I have made a new upgrades: I added additional ram for a total of 32gb and I added an additional 1TB SSD. I do A LOT of photo and video editing and play some more demanding games so I went into the purchase knowing that would be something I would eventually need to do for it to meet my needs, but since the overall bones of the machine were solid, it was a much better option than buying a machine that came with what I wanted out of the box and cost 3x as much.I will say there are two glaring issues with the laptop: the first being the hard drive. Being pitched as a gaming machine with only 256gb storage is a joke. A few meaty games are going to eat that up pretty quickly and you'll start struggling to manage your space. The second is the screen issue. The laptop does have an issue turning on from sleep (or rather it shuts itself off while in sleep, even when plugged in). It will only do this randomly so its a crap shoot on whether holding the power button will actually turn off the laptop and cycle it into a reboot because it was actually just asleep and the screen wasn't turning on, or will just turn it on because it powered itself down for some reason. Its definitely annoying, but I haven't had any issues with it failing to save work so it isn't a deal breaker. These two issues do knock it down a star though.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: This is very much a highly modifiable and budget friendly starter PC. As soon as you look at the hardware you know there are going to be bottleneck points if you want to actually use this for more than 1 modern program. I immediately put it a Predator SSD and upgraded the RAM to 32 bit @ 3200 MHz (two RAM sticks at 16 is going to benefit more than a single 32) which skyrocketed the CPU performance. Every upgrade video you will see show a bunch of adapters that you don't need. There are two (2) M2 ports you can easily access removing the bottom; one hosts the original Hard Drive and the second I put the new SSD drive in, I then followed the Hard Drive copy process on their website and within 10 minutes I was done. It also opened up the bottleneck in the system and allowed games to appropriately use the GPU.Now, the GPU is just midgrade but you get what you pay for. You're not going to play Battlefront / COD at 1080p by any means without a lot of lag, but after just the two upgrades every game so far it flawless at 720p. I could have also lowered the refresh rate from 144 Hz and gotten the responsive 1080p at the cost of smoothing. You can plug in an HDMI-ported high refresh display that bypasses the graphics bottleneck but you got a laptop for a reason and the GPU can still only handle so much.Overall, this is my first time getting a dedicated gaming PC and I'm extremely happy with not only how well it performs but how well laid out it is to modify/upgrade. I would recommend it to people starting out and don't have a high graphics demand.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I am disappointed with this purchase. The product description clearly stated that this HP Victus gaming laptop would feature an Intel Core i5 13th Gen 13420H processor, an NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3050 with 6GB of GDDR6 memory, and 16GB of DDR4-3200 RAM. The listing also highlighted these specifications as key features for 'fast and efficient performance' and 'excellent gaming visuals.'However, the laptop I received is the HP Victus 15-fa0033dx, and the actual specifications are significantly different and inferior to what was advertised:* Processor: Instead of the 13th Gen i5-13420H, it has a 12th Gen Intel Core i5-12450H. As the description itself acknowledges, this is a weaker processor.* Graphics Card: While it does have an RTX 3050, it only has 4GB of GDDR6 VRAM, not the advertised 6GB. This is a crucial difference for gaming performance.* RAM: The received unit has only 8GB of DDR4 RAM, half of the 16GB that was promised, impacting multitasking and potentially gameplay smoothness.The other specifications, such as the 512GB SSD and the 15.6" FHD 144Hz display, appear to be consistent. However, the discrepancies in the processor, GPU VRAM, and RAM are substantial and completely undermine the performance level I expected based on the product description.This is a clear case of misleading information and false advertising. Potential buyers need to be aware that the listed specifications are not what they might receive. The seller absolutely needs to include the specific model number (HP Victus 15-fa0033dx in this case) in their product description to avoid this kind of bait-and-switch.I will be seeking a return/refund due to this significant misrepresentation."

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Great gaming laptop for the price!
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Ive had this laptop for about 2 weeks now. I was nervous buying this because theres so many mixed reviews, but here is my pros and cons and honest opinion (coming from someone who only plays sims and gta5).Ive watched so many Youtube reviews and read so many comments and amazon reviews so it was a very thought out purchase lol.It really has good graphics and runs everything smoothly. Loading times are under 10 seconds no matter what game I am playing.Ive never had a gaming laptop before so i really did my research before buying, and i love this laptop. Light up keyboard, Non flimsy screen (because some people were stating that it wobbles but i dont have a problem with that). battery life does really well and also charges conveniently.All of the features like windows 11 and just the keyboard set up on the laptop is a1 in my opinion. Comes with Omen and Nvidia which just helps you game better. lots of perks with EA and omen discounts steam discounts etc etc.Laptop set up was super simple, downloading apps and things are super easy and fast. I can run my sims game in the background while i google something or watch youtube videos so the ram is nice and i got the 8gb which i was doubting it would be enough ram but its plenty. same for gta5.if youre a casual gamer and still want to have a laptop for day to day basis/ school, i would recommend.i have plenty of storage so far as well. i think it came with 600 gb?? i have about 1000 mods/cc for sims alone with gta and still have a good 500gb left if not more.has bluetooth which i really love to connect my airpods and xbox controller to it. they said it came with an alexa but i havent yet found it or even bothered to look as theres so much to discover when using this and setting up.theres only one or two things ive noticed that i dont like about this laptop but its nothing to not make me buy the laptop again if needed. i noticed your fingerprints are very likely to show all over this laptop lol. outside, mouse pad, screen. lol. nothing to crazy youll just need to wipe often. another thing is the fan is very loud when you have games running. it was noticeable at first because my old laptop wasnt like that but its only because your laptop is processing graphics etc at such a fast pace which is a good thing. i got used to the sound quickly. and the last thing is the mouse pad gets stuck. when i click too much or too hard when gaming it gets pushed down and will get stuck. longest its lasted was like probably less than 5 minutes. just little bit annoying but you can still tap and use mouse any other ways.overall, im really happy with this purchase. its my first gaming laptop let alone brand new out the box and im satisfied with it.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: I thought the reviews were BS, but nah this good
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I genuinely do not understand where the negative reviews are coming from because this is a steal of a laptop. Oh also, the laptop is made of that "not very cheap" plastic which makes it by far the most durable PC I've ever had. Though I am going to still be careful with it of course.I would say that my only criticism would be that the bottom was INCREDIBLY hard to take off which would make it very difficult for repairs, cleaning, and changing hardware. I had to be very gentle at removing it for almost an hour for it to come undone. OH ALSO thank you to whoever decided to put normal Philips head screws on the bottom cause the last 2 laptops I had, had these star shaped ones which were very very annoying.Edit: It has been a bit longer since and I am still rather happy with this laptop. Though I do have a gripe about the keyboard. Ever since I got it, sometimes the laptop will slow down to a very very slow speed (Which is not the end of the world for me, but it is annoying for about 2 minutes) and I cannot seem to find why it is doing it. Other than that, everything is running pretty good and I am still satisfied. Thank you :3

tenido abiertas al mismo tiempo las diferentes tiendas de juegos, páginas web, música en Amazon music y no he tenido ningún problema, sin embargo, decidí comprarle memoria RAM en mi caso 32gb + 4gb de las que ya trae, espero corra aún mejor y sé que estará sobrada.Al principio me preocupo la pantalla, se veían como flashazos muy leves (casi imperceptibles), después de actualizar todos los drivers, Windows, BIOS, etc., ya no volvió a suceder.La pantalla es de 60Hz con 250 nits.El sonido, si bien esta firmado por Bang&Olufsen, no es nada del otro mundo, tenemos que ser conscientes de que es una laptop y el sonido se escucha simplemente decente.Por cierto, en otra opinión se comenta sobre lo de la BIOS, lean esa opinión antes de encender su lap por primera vez.Algunos se quejan de que es muy ruidosa y solo sucede a veces cuando activas el modo rendimiento (aun así, creo que no conocieron las laptops de los años 2000), sin embargo, tu puedes controlar el ventilador (ECO, Silencioso, equilibrado, alto rendimiento)Trae la aplicación OMEN que es excelente para hacer limpieza, personalizar su funcionamiento y optimizar la laptop, se agradece.No trae la letra ñ, pero puedes modificar la disposición del teclado, así como también puedes cambiar el idioma de Windows ya que trae la edición HOME, se tiene que descargar el idioma y después aplicarlo.Efectivamente trae la tarjeta RTX 3050, no la he usado mucho, pero corre muy bien StreetFighter5, CounterStrike, Age of Empires 3 y 4, con gráficos moderados o altos.El procesador es Core i5 12500HCarga muy rápido, en una hora de 80%, si la usas en modo equilibrado te dura 3 horas o más la batería, en alto rendimiento 1 hora.Incluye 1 mes de Microsoft365. 1 mes de McAfee y 1 mes de GamePass.La caja traía un pequeño detalle que no afecto en nada al equipo.No hay muchas reseñas de esta computadora en internet, sin embargo, después de revisar las ACER, ASUS y LENOVO, por sus precios no ofrecen las capacidades de esta (por ejemplo, ampliar la memoria RAM hasta 64GB y el almacenamiento) la recomiendo 100%, yo la compre por 15mil pesos (860USD).

productPageReviewsFromOtherCountries.reviewDescription: Soy de México y para un envío internacional llegó bastante rápido (3 días), el paquete llegó en buen estado en excepción por la caja de Amazon que llegó un poco matrada.Ahora unas recomendaciones para algunas personas en su primer uso y por el que muchas personas tienen problemas con el bitlocker.PRIMER ENCENDIDO DEL DISPOSITIVOEn su primer encendido configurar la configuración básico como se debe, siempre vincular en ese momento una cuenta de Microsoft (Hotmail, outlook) esta parte en la actualidad ya es obligatoria lo digo por que he visto muchas personas que aún no tienen una cuenta de Microsoft en su dispositivo, una ves que logren entrar hasta su escritorio, lo primero que no deben de hacer es irse a su navegador a descargar sus programas de trabajo o sus videojuegos, eso es para después.ACTUALIZACION DEL SISTEMAActualizar el sistema operativo para todos los dispositivos electrónicos debe ser el primer paso que se debe de hacer para un buen funcionamiento, ya que estás actualización quitarán muchos de los problemas en rendimiento, seguridad, etc.Para esto se tienen que ir a la configuración>Windows update, en esta podrán ver las actualizaciones disponibles tendrán que empezar a descargar e instalar, esto se debe de hacer las veces necesarias hasta que ya no aparezcan más actualización.Va a llegar un punto donde el dispositivo actualizará la BIOS y el FIRMWARE, está se instalara de forma diferente desde el recovery del dispositivo (no se espanten si los ventiladores del dispositivo estan al máximo, es normal eso), una ves que de instalen en su reinicio está la posibilidad que de salta la famosa pantalla Bitlocker, si realmente configuraron bien en su primer encendido con una cuenta de Microsoft ya validada, solo tienen que ir a la página que les dice en esa ventana desde otro dispositivo inteligente (otras computadora o celular) solo tienen que iniciar sesión con si cuenta que ingresaron en la computadora al inicio, si todo fue correcto en la página les aparecerá la si clave de recuperación, solo tienen que meterla en la pantalla de Bitlocker (la clave solo de compone de números).Una ves que ya pasaron la ventana del Bitlocker puede que si ingresaron una contraseña para su inicio por seguridad puede que les salte un mensaje que la contraseña no cumple con el formato y no podrán acceder. Esto solo se soluciona ahí mismo, les saltará una ventana de cambio de contraseña, primero les pedirá iniciar sesión con su cuenta de Microsoft por seguridad al cambiar la contraseña, está la pueden cambiar por otra diferente o la misma que tenías. En mi caso cuando se cambió mi contraseña la pantalla se puso en negro posiblemente por los drives de los gráficos, en mi caso solo puse la contraseña en el teclado y me dejó entrar a mi escritorio, como tal es como si se apagará la pantalla pero sigue en la pantalla de bloqueo.Una ves terminado eso, una vez más verifiquen si hay más actualizaciones del sistema y hacer de nuevo las instalaciones necesarias, si ya no aparecen más pues ya puedes irte a tu navegador a descargar tus programas favoritos y tus videojuegos.RENDIMIENTOen cuanto al rendimiento es bastante bueno, una recomendación es que expandan la memoria RAM a 16GB ya que con 8GB se queda corta actualmente.Y esto sería todo por esta reseña espero que les alla sido de ayuda.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Bought this product on sale as a gift for about 650 total. Received it when expected but in packaging that was truly beat to hell. The box was covered in 2 different types of tapes so it’s also entirely possible that with all the craziness of Black Friday the outside-most box just got decimated. No star loss here as the inside box had the appropriate amount of shock resistant packaging material to make it seem protected despite circumstances. I opened the undamaged computer and moved onto the required ssd and ram upgrades and the optional battery upgrade.I wanted to point out that through the Lenovo Vantage app I found out that the battery warranty had already started back in August. From my experience with the Lenovo Legion 5 that period starts once someone registers the product. After searching there is a place to note the date as incorrect and resubmit through the email created alongside the Microsoft one during setup- for people uncomfortable with products that appear to be returned/refurbished be forewarned that appears to be potentially possible. In my case it wasn’t very relevant as you will see. After a more careful inspection I moved on, but nothing in the product description, listing, or packaging made it seem like anything but new. Skip to the end but if you want my attempt at tldr.The required ssd upgrade was a 500gb 2280 NVMe Samsung 970 Evo Plus, the ram was recycled from the above mentioned legion 5 but they are two 8gbs running at 3200m/t from Critical, and optionally I decided to try to port the newish 60wh battery from the legion 5 to replace the 45wh within. The ram and ssd were typical, the laptop came with a baggie of screws that sorta fit the 2280 screw hole but left just a bit of play that does long term worry me will potentially loosen. The battery upgrade did require relocating the bios battery 2/3 inches and the larger battery fit but required some firm but gentle coaxing to sink in its new home. Case closed normally and battery was recognized in Lenovo vantage with normal temps.All upgrades were recognized in the system and after tweaks, updates, and stuff- the attached photo shows the score in user benchmark. If you time the deals correctly the ram and ssd upgrades should be sub 150- even sub 100 if you really got a tight budget. The 60 wh battery can be found 3rd party for a reasonable price as well and with necessary connections, but if you’ll only ever use it plugged in that might not matter. Overall, for the price this laptop can’t be beat as a sub 1k gaming laptop. L4D2 with maxed settings and graphically intense workshop content added barely touches 45% gpu load per Nvidia’s stats. Newer content such as Deep Rock Galactic ran closer to 80-85 fps on maxed settings so playing around with the options/DLSS/reflex boost can yield close to or in excess of the 120hz refresh rate if that matters as well. Overall, 1080p gaming is probably no worries but I didn’t test Crysis so who knows.***The most important thing to say imo is that if you’re unwilling or unable to do the upgrades then I would avoid this computer at any price point.*** The Ryzen 5 gpu hardware reserves 2g of ram by default (disabling the integrated gpu does not yield worthwhile results- don’t bother) and lowering the UMA to 512mb costs more in the computers ability to multitask/multimedia surf effectively. User benchmark proved the performance was worse. That left the free memory on the computer at around 2-3gbs for gaming on the base version which would bottleneck very quickly. Furthermore you definitely want to move windows to whatever 2280 NVMe you upgrade with, the base 256 gb 2242 (or 2246 i forget the size) is adequate but uninspiring and you would benefit from the main system being on the higher bandwidth option- leaving the base storage as overflow.For the DIY capable or willing, this laptop (when upgraded) perfectly captures decent build quality, incredibly cheap price, and capable budget 1080p gaming.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: This was the cheapest laptop with a decent RTX GPU I could find. The system is well balanced with a Ryzen 5 5600H and RTX 3050 ti (mobile). The storage is a 256GB M.2 drive, which is fine for a boot drive, but you will need more storage. It also comes with 8GB of DDR4 RAM. Again, you need more for gaming. It has a white backlit keyboard, no RGB. The screen resolution is 1080P, with a default 120 mhz refresh rate.I ran a passmark bench test first thing, and it severely underperformed. Immediately after that, I installed a 32 GB kit of DDR4. I reran the bench and the scores were dramatically improved. (photo of 2nd test) I didn't have a 2nd storage drive to install, so just the memory upgrade for me. I will say, that is the most important upgrade, and is vital. You need to upgrade the RAM for sure. If you're cheap, you can throw an 8 GB stick in to hit 16, but I suggest buying a 32 GB kit.On a side note, the box seal was missing. (photo) The box was torn where the seal should have been, so it made me wonder if it was used or refurbished. All the packaging inside seemed correct, so I don't know. Something to keep in mind.All in all, If you are comfortable opening a laptop[ for upgrades, this is for you. If you want a ready to go experience, don't do it.
